translation: The jaw bone (頰車骨) is the lower dental arch bone, commonly called the tooth hook (牙釣); it carries the various teeth, can chew food, and has the appearance of movement, hence it is called the jaw (頰車). The tail of this bone is shaped like a hook, controlling upward into the ring of the curved cheek. Whether it is dislocated by a fall or blow, or wind-damp attacks and enters the hook ring causing dislocation, a single dislocation is called a misalignment (錯), and a double dislocation is called a falling out (落).
